PLACES IN THE COMMUNITY LESSON · PLACES IN THE COMMUNITY · AGES 3–5 YEARS

Pharmacy — a step-by-step lesson for grown-up and child

This lesson teaches how medicine travels from doctor to pharmacy to home — and the one rule that rides along.

What is this?

A pharmacy is a shop where medicine is kept and given out by a pharmacist, exactly the amount the doctor ordered.

What does it mean?

Right medicine, right person, right amount: the pharmacist is the town’s medicine referee.

What does the child need to know?

You need the doctor’s paper (the prescription), a grown-up’s hand to carry it in, and patience — good medicine is counted, not rushed.

Why this matters

Medicine is powerful — that is the whole point — so it lives behind the counter with a person who knows exactly how much is right for you.

What it teaches

Understanding "medicine is not candy", waiting at a counter, naming helpers (doctor writes, pharmacist fills, grown-up gives), and the safety habit for life.

Words to learn

pharmacydrugstorechemistpharmacistprescriptionmedicinecounterdose

Say this to your child

“"Here is the doctor’s paper! The pharmacist reads it, counts the medicine — one, two, three — and writes my name on the bottle. Medicine rides home with a grown-up. That is the rule, and it keeps me safe!"”

Step by step

  1. The doctor writes a paper — the prescription — just for you.
  2. A grown-up hands the paper over the pharmacy counter.
  3. The pharmacist counts and pours: exactly the right amount, no more.
  4. The label gets your name on it — read it together: that says YOU.
  5. The bag goes home with the grown-up, and the grown-up gives the medicine — that is the one rule, said kindly, every time.

Look closer at the picture

On the card, the cross shines above the pharmacy windows — in many towns this is the shop whose lights stay on latest, because helpers close last.

Ask your child

"Who fills the prescription?" (the pharmacist) "Whose name goes on the label?" (yours) "Who gives the medicine at home?" (a grown-up — always)

What your child can say or do

Your child might sort pom-pom "medicine" into bottles with hospital-grade seriousness, stamp every doll label with their own name, or recite the safety rule to the cat unprompted — repeat customers are the goal.

Out in the real world

American families say drugstore; British families say chemist’s or pharmacy — the counter works the same everywhere. Pharmacists answer questions for free, and many will show a child the counting tray if asked at a quiet moment.

Try it together

Pharmacy at home: colored pom-poms in pill bottles, sorted by color and size, labels drawn on with names. One rule repeated kindly while playing — medicine is only for grown-ups to give.

Understanding check

Ask: "Who counts the medicine?" (the pharmacist) "And who gives it to you at home?" (a grown-up — never yourself, never from the bottle)

This lesson pairs with the Pharmacy flashcard in the library — print it, show it, keep it on the fridge. Back to Places in the Community.
